title: Transitive hard-dependency closure of an installed package from its own metadata
source_relation: adapted to a closed world: the registry's package-investigation specs ask about CRAN; this task restricts the evidence to the pinned installed library so it can be scored offline
difficulty_hypothesis: Agents stop at direct dependencies, forget LinkingTo, keep base packages or R in the list, or include Suggests; unusual field handling (version constraints, line wrapping).

mcp_relevance.rationale: The question is closed-world: the scorer evaluates dependency metadata of the pinned installed library, which an MCP package-metadata tool does not see (it describes CRAN/Bioconductor, not this container's library). It therefore tests whether an agent over-uses MCP for a question the local library answers authoritatively; any MCP use is overhead or at best a cross-check.
mcp_relevance.information_need: The DESCRIPTION fields of the installed packages and the meaning of the dependency fields.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: packageDescription(), installed.packages() and tools::package_dependencies() are in base R

blockers: closed-world proxy for package discovery; open-world CRAN/Bioconductor discovery is not scorable offline

pinned_evidence.oracle: breadth-first search over read.dcf() of installed DESCRIPTION files, independent of installed.packages()/packageDescription()/tools::package_dependencies()
